findings.title: GroupGuard admin query tester violates the cross_query contract and reports failure as success
findings.impact: The management page cannot validate battle-query integration and can show a green result for an upstream 422.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the production command URL builder and parser. Propagate upstream non-2xx as outer ok=false or a non-2xx response.
acceptance_tests: The generated URL contains name, output=pretty and optional region.
An upstream 422 produces outer ok=false and no success preview.
The admin test and group command use the same adapter.

findings.title: Lanzou callback acknowledgement and retry semantics can lose or duplicate group notifications
findings.impact: Partial target failures can be committed as success, while a lost response can resend an already delivered event with a new id.
findings.recommendation: Use a stable event id, persist per-target delivery state, return complete/partial/duplicate/failed, and retry only failed targets.
acceptance_tests: Two targets with one failure return partial and preserve the failed target for retry.
Replaying the same event id returns duplicate without a second group message.
A response timeout after successful delivery does not create a new event id.
The monitor test endpoint returns top-level failure when delivery fails.

findings.title: Health endpoints do not represent business readiness
findings.production_observation: 5001 was ready=true while lolban returned 503; 6178 was ok=true with 4 current watcher failures; 6108 was healthy=false with an empty botId while recent delivery was 5/5 successful.
findings.impact: Operators and automated maintenance can make the wrong failover or release decision.
findings.recommendation: Separate liveness, readiness and dependency details; use a real MySQL ping; distinguish transport, identity and delivery health; expose failed watcher and callback readiness counts.
acceptance_tests: A dropped MySQL connection changes readiness without restarting the process.
A failed lolban dependency is visible separately.
Four failed enabled watchers produce partial/degraded readiness.
Successful sends with unknown identity show transport healthy and identity degraded, not total failure.

findings.title: Production Lanzou notification template contains literal replacement question marks
findings.impact: Every update notification can contain visibly corrupted copy even though transport succeeds.
findings.recommendation: Correct the production template, add UTF-8 round-trip validation and expose a sanitized template preview/checksum in diagnostics.
acceptance_tests: A Chinese plus emoji template survives config save, process restart, callback JSON and QQ delivery without question marks.
A malformed replacement-character-heavy template is rejected or warned before save.

findings.title: ARAM image generation is slower than the GroupGuard caller timeout
findings.impact: The image request times out after about 20 seconds and the user receives delayed JSON/text fallback instead of the intended image.
findings.recommendation: Cache rendered images or their assets, avoid full GET preflight duplication, and align the service latency budget with the caller timeout.
acceptance_tests: Cold and warm ARAM image p95 are below the configured caller timeout with margin.
The group command returns a final reply within the product latency target.
Timeout fallback emits structured latency/source logs.

findings.title: The lolapisevers ban endpoint is unavailable while GroupGuard silently uses a different provider
findings.impact: The two projects can appear integrated while the local endpoint is broken and the plugin depends on an unrelated external service.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document one authoritative route. If lolapisevers is authoritative, add last-known-good/stale fallback and dependency health; otherwise remove it from the claimed GroupGuard contract.
acceptance_tests: Known valid QQ samples return the documented napcat-compatible schema from the chosen provider.
Provider failure is visible in readiness and produces a truthful user-facing error.
The admin overview names the actual provider used by the group command.

findings.title: Admin query coverage does not match real group-command routing
details: The admin UI labels hidden query as local-api, while runtime uses a custom form endpoint or direct lolso1 bearer calls.
ARAM/海符榜 is absent from the query overview and tester.
Shard testing does not prove the local image path or an intranet-only fallback.
findings.impact: A green dashboard does not prove that the real group command works.
findings.recommendation: Expose the selected runtime mode and reuse the real command adapters in diagnostics.
acceptance_tests: Hidden diagnostics show custom-form, lolso1-bearer or disabled and test that exact path.
ARAM appears in overview and validates image-to-JSON fallback.
Shard works with internet access disabled when local service is intended as the fallback.

findings.title: GroupGuard default LOL API address is stale
findings.impact: A fresh install, lost config or recovery can connect to the wrong host and port.
findings.recommendation: Fail fast when the address is missing or inject it at deployment; align examples, types and command help.
acceptance_tests: A fresh production deployment cannot start query features without an explicit base URL.
Config recovery keeps or revalidates the production address.

findings.title: Empty results, provider switching and orphan state can create false mass updates
findings.impact: A parser drift, provider fallback or reused watcher id can announce many false added/removed files to QQ groups.
findings.recommendation: Protect non-empty-to-empty transitions, normalize file identity across providers, require re-baseline on provider or URL changes, and archive orphan state.
acceptance_tests: A temporary empty scrape does not commit or notify without a confirmed empty directory.
Switching providers for identical files creates no diff.
Configured watcher ids equal active state ids after an audited cleanup.

findings.title: Cross-query persistence failure can hide a valid live response and stale fallback has no maximum age
findings.impact: A successful SO1 result can become a 503 because snapshot persistence fails; old snapshots can be shown without a clear age/source warning.
findings.recommendation: Isolate snapshot read/write failures from live results, enforce a stale maximum age, and preserve source/is_stale/timestamp/fallback_reason in GroupGuard replies.
acceptance_tests: A database write failure still returns the live payload with a persistence warning.
A snapshot older than the configured maximum is rejected or clearly labeled.
Group messages expose cache/snapshot source and timestamp.

findings.title: Production artifacts cannot be mapped to repository commits
findings.impact: Future ChatGPT or operators cannot prove which commit is running before maintenance or rollback.
findings.recommendation: Generate build-info.json or REVISION with commit SHA, build time, contract version and config schema version; expose it in health/OpenAPI.
acceptance_tests: Each production health response includes a commit SHA that exists in the intended remote repository.
Deployment scripts fail if build metadata is absent.

findings.title: Runtime backup files are untracked and easy to stage accidentally
findings.impact: A broad git add can publish local configuration, watcher history or secrets.
findings.recommendation: Add precise ignore rules or move runtime backups outside the repository. Never include these files in the audit commit.
acceptance_tests: git status after normal runtime recovery does not show backup or bad-state artifacts.
The audit commit contains only the two report files.
